issue_context.title: A potential bug of NPD
issue_context.body:
Hi, I found a potential null pointer dereference bug in the project source code of openssl, and I have shown the execution sequence of the program that may generate the bug on the graph below. The red text illustrates the steps that generate the bug, the red arrows represent the call relationships, the file path can be seen in the blue framed section.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/87304478/186350353-da45a094-2fee-4910-a8c0-817fb88b5fc8.png)
Although the code shown is for version 1.1.1, this potential bug is still present in the current version
https://github.com/openssl/openssl/blob/bf16ee4f95c31a66e76056c691f25a0d2b4a39c4/apps/speed.c#L3483-L3487

would you can help to check if this bug is true?thank you!
comments: Looks like a bug.  Given where it is I don't believe it has a security impact but it should still be fixed.

Upon further investigation, I don't think this can trigger.  It's parsing a string produced by code in the same file.
It's fragile nonetheless.

There are a lot of other cases of this using both atoi and atof.

review_comments: This doesn't look great.  sstrsep can set p to NULL and you removed the initial NULL check so it will fail if so.  So crashy times with malformed data.
@paulidale `sstrsep` can return empty string, but not NULL (if its argument is not NULL).
